newsitem.title: KENYA: Weather seen undermining Kenya tea results.
newsitem.headline: Weather seen undermining Kenya tea results.

text.p: Kenya's total 1996 tea production figure may be undermined by poor weather, a leading brokerage said on Wednesday.
"Crop figures for the month of November are below projections due to wet weather which prevailed for most of the month," the Mombasa-based Africa Tea Brokers (ATB) said in its report for December.
It posted November production at 20,493,490 kg, an increase of 906,581 kg over the same month in 1995.
It added that the cumulative production figure at end-November stood at 233.65 kg, an increase of 11.18 million kg over the previous year.
But crop analysts said weather patterns meant 1996 output could fall short of the 246 million kg reached in 1995.

Four sales were held during November in which a total of 241,147 packages were sold at an average price of $1.52 compared to three sales in November 1995 when 205,627 packages were sold at an average price of $1.39.
Pakistan, Egypt, Sudan, Yemen, Britain, the Commonwealth of Independent States, South Africa and North America were the main buyers. Somalia bought lower-priced teas.
